name: Start with Duration 100: Started and done at once; advanced 100, Finished lands
because: timer.ts :59-61; timerscheduler.ts :185-190 (delay 0 starts at once), :139-141 and :156-159 (t >= 1 finishes). NSP-007 AC2, the firing arm

name: Start with Duration 100, advanced only 99: Started, done, and NO Finished (the absence beside the firing arm)
because: NSP-007 AC2 — an absence asserted beside a known-firing control (the scenario above); timerscheduler.ts :156-157 t < 1 stays running

name: Duration 0 and no Start Delay: Started in one frame, Finished in the NEXT, with no time passing
because: timerscheduler.ts :177-197 — a queued timer joins after the frame's pass, so its first read is the next frame (:130-159, t = 1 for duration 0)

name: Stop while queued: reports unchanged, yet the countdown is cancelled — no Started ever (D10)

name: Stop while running: done, and Finished never fires for it
because: timer.ts :103-108; timerscheduler.ts :96-107 leaves the running set; :158 `!_wasStopped`

name: Start Delay 50, Duration 0: nothing until the clock passes 50, then Started AND Finished in one frame

name: Restart while running: done, and Started fires again at the next frame
because: timer.ts :71-77; timerscheduler.ts :43-50 stop() then scheduleTimer; :52-57 _hasCalledOnStart false

name: raw arithmetic: a string Duration '5' counts down 5 ms; a null Duration is t = 1 and finishes at the next frame
